anchors.paper_title: Electroencephalography‐Based Clustering Reveals Robust Neurophysiological Subtypes in Parkinson's Disease
anchors.reason: The candidate paper's title and abstract describe the analysis of EEG recordings obtained from 116 PD patients and 30 healthy controls, matching the exact cohort and modality of the dataset.

metadata.methods_description: EEG data were acquired using a 64-channel Geodesic EEG System 400 (EGI system) with electrode montage following the International 10–20 system. Recordings were conducted under two conditions: resting state (sitting, eyes open, ~4 minutes) and walking on a treadmill at comfortable speed (~4 minutes). Clinical assessments included demographic data, Levodopa Equivalent Daily Dose (LEDD), Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Movement Disorder Society Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (MDS-UPDRS), and Color Trails Test (CTT).

citation_details.title: PD-EEG: Resting-State & Walking EEG in Parkinson's Disease
citation_details.author: Zoya Katzir, Daniel Vered, Inbal Maidan (inbalm@tlvmc.gov.il)
citation_details.abstract: This dataset comprises 64-channel EEG recordings from 116 Parkinson's disease patients and 28 healthy controls acquired during resting state (sitting, eyes open) and treadmill walking conditions. Each participant underwent approximately 4 minutes of EEG recording under both behavioral conditions, with accompanying clinical assessments including MDS-UPDRS, MoCA, and medication dosage data. The dataset was collected at the Neurology Institute, Tel Aviv Sourasky Medical Center, and is organized according to BIDS specifications.

citation_details.title: Walking-State Geometry Separates Parkinson Disease from Controls More Clearly Than Paired Rest-to-Walk Reconfiguration
citation_details.author: Robin Langell
citation_details.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
citation_details.abstract: The walking EEG export ds007526 contains two different inference problems that should not be forced into one coordinate contract. PD walk vs HC walk is a between-subject disease-state question and is therefore evaluated here in cohort_anchored space, whereas PD walk vs rest is a within-subject task-reconfiguration question and is therefore evaluated in subject_anchored space. We analyzed 277 processed runs from 144 participants (116 Parkinson disease, 28 healthy controls), using the refreshed bundle data/raw/neuralmanifolddynamics_ds007526_20260610_121725. In the base standard family, BH-FDR q < 0.05 retained 4 cohort-walk rows, 3 Parkinson paired rows, and 1 healthy-control paired context row. The cohort-walk headline was concentrated in the d family: global walk d_n_mean (d = 0.766, q = 0.030), d_n_median (d = 0.746, q = 0.030), d_mean (d = 0.711, q = 0.036), and d_median (d = 0.718, q = 0.036). A targeted subject-anchor dispersion extension that added within-run IQR and MAD summaries sharpened the paired Parkinson branch more strongly than the original central-tendency-only pass, led by m_a_iqr (d_z = 0.472, q = 6.55e-4), d_iqr (d_z = 0.403, q = 7.28e-4), d_mad (d_z = 0.412, q = 7.28e-4), together with d_n_mean (d_z = 0.409, q = 7.28e-4). The secondary healthy-control paired context remained dominated by m_a_mean (d_z = 0.888, q = 0.0176). The same dispersion extension also revealed strong rest-side clinical associations, especially global d_s_iqr with age (rho = -0.377, q = 8.38e-4) and CTT (rho = -0.351, q = 0.00489), plus parietal-occipital e_iqr with CTT (rho = 0.439, q = 1.25e-4). Supplement-level supportive layers still showed a rest-weighted global reachability branch and an exploratory compact-summary trajectory layer. The present bundle did not expose conventional_eeg, so no classical comparator claim is made. Within this export surface, walking in a cohort-shared frame separates Parkinson disease from controls more clearly than paired rest-to-walk reconfiguration, but the paired Parkinson branch becomes materially stronger once dispersion summaries are included

citation_details.title: Instantaneous-Frequency EEG Microstate Dynamics Stratify Motor Subtypes in Parkinson’s Disease
citation_details.author: Sou Nobukawa, Hirohisa Watanabe
citation_details.abstract: Abstract Parkinson’s disease (PD) is clinically heterogeneous, yet objective electrophysiological markers of its postural-instability/gait-difficulty (PIGD) and tremor-dominant (TD) motor subtypes are lacking. We tested whether the temporal dynamics of instantaneous-frequency (IF) microstates in resting-state electroen-cephalography (EEG) distinguish these subtypes from each other and from healthy controls (HC). In a publicly available cohort (OpenNeuro ds007526) comprising 28 HC and 97 PD patients classified as PIGD (n = 50) or TD (n = 47), the spatial distribution of the IF was reduced by principal component analysis and modeled with a Gaussian hidden Markov model, yielding three recurrent microstates. Per-participant mean dwell time, occupancy, and state-transition probabilities were compared across the three groups and, within PD, correlated with clinical scores. We found that the dynamics of one microstate varied systematically across groups: its dwell time, occupancy, and self-transition probability increased monotonically from HC through TD to PIGD, while outgoing transitions decreased, so that the state became an increasingly persistent attractor. For dwell time, all three pairwise contrasts survived correction (HC versus PIGD, Hedges’ g = 1.06; HC versus TD, g = 0.59; PIGD versus TD, g = 0.40). None of the dynamic indices was associated with clinical severity, disease duration, or medication dose within PD. IF-microstate dynamics thus stratify the PD motor subtypes along a graded continuum without tracking continuous disease severity. The approach offers a candidate objective EEG marker for motor-subtype stratification, complementing spectral characterizations of PD.
